title: Prove Yazelix Astra as a thin orchestrator
description:
Goal:
Prove the smallest useful Yazelix product assembled from accepted Orbit, Venus, Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig artifacts while preserving one owner for each behavior.

Scope boundary:
This epic is planning-only until the user activates the Astra implementation frontier. Do not add runtime code, installers, CI, package manifests, compatibility layers, or duplicate child behavior while it remains deferred. Yazelix Nova remains independent.

Contracts:
AST-C1 through AST-C7.

Sequence:
1. Orbit proves the session and client-facing contracts Astra needs.
2. Venus proves useful native interaction against an accepted Orbit revision.
3. The user explicitly activates Astra.
4. Astra proves one composed Linux slice, then distribution parity and macOS.

Success:
Astra stays a small policy, composition, diagnostics, and distribution owner. Exact child revisions, relocatable artifacts, and checks prove the product without creating a second terminal, renderer, editor, file manager, or configuration system.

title: Activate Astra after Orbit and Venus prove integration revisions
description:
Decision gate:
Do not begin Astra implementation until the user explicitly activates this bead.

Required evidence:
- Orbit names and proves the session, attachment, transport, and recovery contracts that Venus and Astra consume.
- Venus proves useful native interaction against an exact accepted Orbit revision.
- Both projects publish or produce relocatable artifacts for the selected target.
- No known P0 or P1 defect invalidates the boundary.
- The user chooses Astra as the active implementation frontier.

Acceptance:
Record exact Orbit and Venus revisions, proven contract IDs, verification commands, platforms, artifact locations and checksums, known limitations, and the user activation decision. Confirm that work on the previous frontier has reached its agreed handoff boundary.

Scope:
This bead approves a frontier. It does not implement Astra.

title: Define the canonical Astra component manifest
description:
Contracts:
AST-C2 and AST-C3.

Goal:
Define one small, human-reviewable manifest that pins exact child revisions and relocatable artifacts for every supported target. Direct bundles, Nix, Home Manager, and later channels must consume this same graph.

Reference and tool gate:
Inspect current child release metadata, cargo-dist, GitHub immutable releases, Nix bundle, and at least one comparable multi-component product manifest. Compare a hand-owned schema, existing release tooling, and no added tool. Record versions, maintenance, platform fit, license, supply-chain posture, local LOC, and exit conditions.

Acceptance:
- The schema names project, revision, contract version, target, artifact, checksum, provenance, and launch inputs.
- A focused validator rejects incompatible or incomplete sets.
- A relocatability check finds machine-local and undeclared Nix store references.
- One fixture pins accepted Orbit and Venus artifacts plus Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md records exact proof evidence.

Scope:
Do not create a second dependency graph for any package manager and do not rebuild child behavior in Astra.

title: Prove the smallest useful Astra Linux composition
description:
Contracts:
AST-C1 and AST-C4.

Goal:
Prove one usable Linux vertical slice from the canonical component manifest: yzx launches an accepted Venus and Orbit pair, exposes Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig through their owned contracts, preserves one configuration path, and reports exact component versions.

Before code:
Review the accepted child contracts and exact proof revisions. State the process tree, configuration ownership, failure behavior, and cheapest integration check. Run the crate and tool gate for every proposed runtime dependency.

Acceptance:
- A clean user environment can launch, use, detach, reattach, and stop the composed session.
- yzx exposes a diagnostic version report tied to the component manifest.
- Restart and partial-child-failure checks preserve declared user state.
- Astra contains policy and adapters only; ownership review finds no copied terminal, rendering, editor, file-manager, or Ratconfig state.
- Fresh-session dogfood records the exact artifact and limitations.

Scope:
Keep the first slice narrow. Sidebars, popups, plugin surfaces, legacy compatibility, and extra package channels require user decisions.

title: Design and prove the direct Linux release bundle
description:
Contract:
AST-C5.

Goal:
Ship the proven Linux component set as a relocatable archive with an inspectable installation path that does not require Nix.

Reference and tool gate:
Compare cargo-dist, a small owned assembler, and other maintained tools that can consume the canonical manifest. Inspect archive reproducibility, checksums, signatures or attestations, installer generation, rollback, uninstall, multi-architecture support, dependency weight, and local LOC.

Acceptance:
- Publish an immutable archive, checksum, and signature or attestation for each accepted Linux target.
- Support manual extraction plus an installer with dry-run, versioned user prefix, atomic current link, upgrade, rollback, and removal.
- Preserve user data and avoid unrequested shell-profile edits.
- Verify on a clean user environment and record artifact size and closure contents.
- Prepare yazelix.com installation copy without making the website the binary authority.

Scope:
AppImage, Flatpak, deb, rpm, containers, and system repositories stay outside this bead.

title: Prove Nix and Home Manager parity with direct Astra releases
description:
Contract:
AST-C6.

Goal:
Keep Nix and Home Manager as optional first-class channels over the canonical component manifest and prove that they run the same product as the direct bundle.

Acceptance:
- Nix and Home Manager consume the same exact component revisions and compatibility metadata as the direct release.
- Version diagnostics match across channels.
- Runtime behavior and configuration ownership remain channel-independent.
- A clean profile and Home Manager evaluation pass without requiring the direct installer.
- Documentation presents Nix as an option instead of an Astra runtime prerequisite.

Scope:
Do not maintain a Nix-only component graph, runtime contract, or feature.

title: Design and prove native macOS Astra distribution
description:
Contract:
AST-C7.

Goal:
Distribute the accepted Astra component set through a native macOS boundary owned with Venus.

Reference and tool gate:
Review Apple signing and notarization requirements, Homebrew Cask, universal and architecture-specific artifact tradeoffs, application bundle layout, quarantine behavior, PTY and process assumptions, and candidate release tooling. Record cost, required credentials, platform support, local LOC, and exit conditions.

Acceptance:
- Produce a signed and notarized application or disk image for the selected architectures.
- Publish a Homebrew Cask over the same immutable artifacts and component manifest.
- Verify Gatekeeper, quarantine, first launch, upgrade, version diagnostics, and removal on a clean macOS user account.
- Record every Linux assumption that required a boundary or child fix.

Scope:
Do not simulate native distribution with a Linux-only package foundation.
